title: GM Monti Ossenfort And HC Mike LaFleur Address The Media After Day 2 Of NFL Draft | AZ Cardinals
text: Um started off the day at 34 taking Chase Basantis out of Texas A&M. Uh you know throughout the day today had a lot of uh a lot of phone calls. There was a lot of interest in pick 34. Um you know we had at you know different at different times six seven eight teams we're interested in coming up. Um you know nothing uh nothing really came close to getting us to move off that pick. We're excited to add Chase. Um big physical player out of&M played against a lot of good people there. uh really in practice blocking his own D lineman that he had to block there for the last three years and then in the SEC obviously high level of uh competition. So excited to add Chase. And then just now just a little bit ago um at the top of the third round um 65 um again had had a little bit of trade interest, not as much as 34. Um and then took Carson back there at the the top of the third round. So, you know, Carson uh has played a lot of football, played, uh, you know, two-year starter at Georgia, won a lot of games there, had some success, uh, and then, you know, obviously this year goes down and and and has a heck of a year for Miami. Uh, takes him to the the national championship, saw him play out here in the semi-finals, a Fiesta Bowl. So, um, you know, excited to add those two players and then, uh, we got, uh, what, four picks coming up tomorrow early in the fourth round. We'll kick it off tomorrow morning. So, with that, we'll open it up for you, with you guys. What really sold you with Carson back? >> Yeah, I think, you know, we spent a lot of time with Carson. Um, you know, we met with him at the combine. Um, brought him in on a 30 visit. Um, you know, there was no shortage of tape to evaluate on Carson. Um, Carson's played a lot of ball. Um, and so, you know, banked a lot of reps. Um, you know, I think really, uh, Carson's, uh, Carson played in a lot of big game environments. um played in a lot of intense environments in um in the SEC, those stadiums, those loud screaming, wild, rabid fans of the SEC. Um and then, you know, the the highest stage that he could play on in the national championship this year, all those playoff games. Um you know, I think a lot of things sold us sold us on Carson and we were excited to add him to our room. >> What What did he show you in that in that Fiesta Bowl game that you said you were at? Obviously, when you're there in person, I'm sure you could see it a little bit differently. So, what did he prove to you? >> Yeah, really. I mean, there's no uh no bigger opportunities than national semi-final, you know, and so to be able to answer the bell, lead his team, uh bring him down there. It was a tight game. Um you know, and so uh Carson's been productive whole step of his way uh a whole step of his career at different spots and you know that that game was no different. >> How does how does him transferring from Miami or from Georgia to Miami, how can that help with his transition to to year? Yeah, I think I think it's a great transition because he's about to do another one. So, he's going to have to um you know, he picked up the G from the Georgia program, goes to a new locker room, has to you know, learn a new offense, learn a new system, learn new verbiage, learn a new building, and then most importantly, learn new teammates. And so, um he's about to do the same thing here in a couple weeks when he gets here. And, um so, it's, you know, he's got a good practice run of it. Do you see a scenario where Carson could compete for a starting position or is you know >> Yeah, I you know I think like we just announced his name about a half hour ago. So, you know, I we just want to get him in the building here and show him where the cafeteria is and the locker room is and and uh and get him fitted for his gear and and then we'll we'll go from there. We're excited to add be great competition in that room and and we'll see how it shakes out. >> Mike made about his struggles when pressured statistically. what made you kind of willing to overlook that in terms of his prospect profile? >> I mean, you know, listen, hey, we we look at everything with the player. Um, you know, a lot has been made. I, you know, I don't know. We we look at the tape and and we evaluate him and his performance and the guy's performed. The guy's won a lot of games and we were we were excited to add him. >> What was it specifically about kind of his skill set? I know you mentioned the experience, but about his skill set that kind of sold you on him. >> Uh, he's big, he's tough, he's strong, he's standing strong in the pocket. uh not afraid to to take a hit in the pocket. He's got a good good arm strength. He can drive the ball down the field. Um good accuracy, good production. Um you know, those are all things that we like. >> To you, Mike, >> what's it out to you with the back mic? >> I think a lot of the things that Monty was just saying. You know, he is a he's a big solid dude, right? I mean, he's 6'4, he's 235 pounds. I mean, he looks the part, right? And that that doesn't, you know, mean that that's the end all beall by any means. uh natural thrower like he was just saying he's tough. I think one of the coolest things about him, especially spending some time with them, um, you know, he's been through those big games, but he's he's been through some adversity, too, you know, and, uh, and that's well documented, you know, it's out there. And, um, I think he's gotten better from it. You know, I wasn't there, you know, through that journey through the last few years, but, uh, just being able to get to know him and really spend some time. I really enjoyed my time with him. I know Monty did as well. I know our building did. So, um, there's a lot of cool things that, uh, we're excited about, you know, working with him. [snorts] >> With Chase, how does he fit into what you guys want to do offensively? >> Yeah. You want to go? >> Go ahead. You got it. >> Yeah. No. Um, Chase is is what you want in a guard. He can move. He can cover people up. Uh, but ultimately, he strains to finish, you know, and that's what you really like about him. Um, he's willing to work. Justin Fry has known him for a long time. He actually recruited him. um obviously didn't pick Justin, but uh uh at the time, but now he has no choice. So, uh but no, they've had a relationship for a long time. Justin, um like I said, I mean, he's he's known the guy, the person, where he came from. Uh so, you think about just the attributes I was talking about. You think about the finish and then and then the guy um good uh you know, good mix. >> Envision him as a guard or he played right tackle as a freshman. So, would you move him over? He >> he did and that's cool, right? I mean, he had the the one year starting at right tackle, then be able to move in inside for the uh the last two yards or two yards two years. Um, so I mean, you see him in the inside, but I mean, you know how it is in this league. Sometimes you you don't got the choice, but yeah, he'll be starting inside initially. >> You expect him to start on the right side with Isaac Sale on the left or or still working through, >> you know, it's still working through all those kind of things because particularly in again in the NFL with the with the roster limits and then once you obviously get down to game time. So, um, you know, he'll he'll be on the right side, he'll be on the left side, and we'll figure out what the best five are going to end up being. [snorts] >> Monty, with all the changes that you've made, all the additions you've made on the offensive line, including Chase, do you like how that position room is trending right now? >> I do. Yeah, I do. Whenever we can add size, physicality, toughness, um, competition. I mean, we've seen we've seen what happens when when, uh, attrition of the NFL season happens. So, um, whenever we can add big physical players up front, um, you know, we're always going to take advantage of doing that. with with Carson. He played a lot of football, six years in college, 43 starts. Where could it help him kind of slow down, sit for a little bit and learn from the vets that you guys have right now? >> Yeah. Well, and he's had to do that in his career, too, right? I mean, he was a backup to a guy that I know really well in Stson Bennett. Um, so yeah, I mean, I, you know, it benefits anyone in any position to be able to sit back. Sometimes guys don't have the choice, you know, because you have to put your best 22 out on the field there, you know. Um, so we'll see where this thing all shakes out, but we're just excited, like you said. I mean, just want to get him here and show him his locker and get to know his teammates and and and get working from day one and we'll see where it goes from there. >> Monty, was it a priority for you entering this draft at a quarterback? >> Uh, priority? I mean, no, I don't think so. Um, you know, you know, we've we've talked about it. We never want to force a pick. And, um, you know, ultimately at 65, uh, Carson was was a great fit for us at that point. Um if if it wouldn't have worked out then we would have went on to the next guy. >> You mentioned his big game experience quite a bit. Where does that ring for you in terms of when you evaluate a player? >> Yeah. I mean I think uh you know I think uh when you when you see a player who has had big game experience um you know when they make this transition to the NFL uh there's a little there's more hope that it's not going to be too big for him, right? So, it's not going to be a deer in the headlights or I mean, you know, the these guys have played that have played at these high levels, especially, you know, SEC um and then into the ACC, these Big 10 programs, like they're these stadiums are rocking and they go into hostile environments and so I think that's always good. I mean, the NFL there's no bigger stage and so I think the trans transition is a little bit smoother for them. >> You guys have not made a ton of moves uh so far this offseason on the defensive side of the ball. what kind of makes you feel like that group can elevate uh kind of from where it was last year to this upcoming season with the lack of um offseason investment so far? Yeah, I mean I think you know with as we've always talked I mean it's um whether it's free agency or the draft like the the fit has to match up and so um you know it's it's you you have to it's a balance of depending on young player development uh to play depending on players getting healthy. Um and then also um you know like just like last year when when we sat in here and we we took all the uh all the defensive players you know that wasn't that wasn't a plan you know it's just how it worked out. And so today we've gone and we picked uh last two days we picked three offensive players. That's just how it worked out. So um you know I think we'll we'll see what happens tomorrow. We got four picks. Um but you know I think it's it's a combination of what's available whether it's free for agency or the draft and then what meets with our the resources that we have. >> How does drafting Carson now affect your approach with Jacobe? >> Uh I don't think it really does. I think it's completely independent. Um you know excited to add Carson in. He's going to have two veterans um to work with that have played a lot of football. Um and really I think those are two independent things. >> You guys rushing attack rank near the bottom of the league last year and obviously you talked about drafting best player available whenever it comes to it, but uh Jeremiah Love and then Bantis like was it a cognizant effort by you guys to try to improve the run game heading to 2025? Donnie, yeah, I think it was just a cognious effort to just improve our team in general and, you know, that that can look different and uh it doesn't always, you know, like you can have a plan, but then um where where the draft lines up, it it you know, that's where it takes you. And so, um I think we're just always in in in the lane of hey, we want to improve our team, we want to add talent, we want to improve competition. Um and the way it's felt, it's just been on offense so far the last two days. Um, Chase has not allowed a sack for either one of you guys in his last 18 games. >> That's a That's good to hear, Josh. I >> like that, man. That's Let's keep that going. [laughter] Person that goes through your head in terms of your evaluation of a player that >> Yeah, he he's a tough dude. And I think in both phases, um, you know, he has the ability to get it done. And, you know, kind of like we were just saying with Carson, I mean, he's he's played some pretty good football, too, right? you know, at Texas A&M in the SEC going against obviously a lot of good rushers, whether it be interior or on the edge. So, um, again, just just a guy that, uh, excited to work with in terms of the talent level, but again, the the the toughness is really what sticks out to me. >> His athletic profile is pretty impressive when you look at the speed and strength. What can that do for an offense? Kind of what >> what does that enable you to do as a play caller, I guess, especially? Yeah, I mean it's, you know, you want guys that can move, you know, whether it's just in the protection and and the slides and the man and and all that kind of stuff, but particularly in the run game can get connected at the second level, but again, I don't think that's just, you know, he's he's powerful enough to reach a guy and anchor and he's also, you know, u I would say has the ability to get to the second level and latch and and and drive, you know. So, um, again, just just excited to get working with them. >> [snorts] >> A lot of uh quarterbacks land in the NFL. Sometimes it might not be a good schematic for him. Obviously, you know what you want to do, but we really don't. What can you say about what Carson Beck can fit inside like your offense like specifically? >> You know, it's it's cool cuz you can evaluate his tape at Georgia and Miami, all the things that we've been talking about, the big game experience, all those kind of things. But he's run what you would say quote unquote an NFL style system. you know, you watch the the Miami National Championship game and you have to see him clicking through progressions against a really good defense in Indiana, you know, so um for him, you know, it's it's nothing against any other quarterbacks. It's just he was given the opportunity to kind of be in more a similar system as to what most NFL um you know, offenses do. I know you said it wasn't necessarily intentional to draft a quarterback, but when you've got not just someone like Jacobe, but Jacobe who's been in the league for 10 years and as as strong of a leader as he is, does that give you maybe like reassurance of knowing what as a rookie Carson Beck who he's going to be sharing that room with and learning from? >> Yeah, I mean, Danny, I think like absolutely. And I think we have a lot of good veterans. I mean, you we've seen some of our players have reached out to us about when we when we take a player. um people, our players have reached out and congratulated our rookies already or the guys that we've drafted already. And you know, I think that's big for our locker room in general, just having um having veterans that are willing to reach out and have it show the example and show what it means to be a pro. Um so, you know, our quarterback room, our running back room, our O line room, they all got three new players to work with and I know they're going to embrace those three.

title: Zachariah Branch speaks to the media after being drafted by the Atlanta Falcons | 2026 NFL Draft
text: the staff here was um highly complimentary of how um their pre-draft stuff with you was. I mean, when did you meet with them and how did your interactions with them kind of unfold? >> Yes. Uh you know, I had a I had a meeting with them um you know, earlier this month, I would say. Actually, not earlier, not really not too long ago. Um you know, probably like maybe a week and some change ago. um you know went up there to the visit and I had a great time just talking with the staff you know bonded with a lot of them uh you know just personalitywise and just connecting on a personal level not even talking about football which is something I loved and I feel like I can be myself you know in their building that was something that was really important um but I was very grateful for the opportunity um and then you know talking football just the way that you know they approach the game and how they go about their culture and everything like that is something that um you know I'm very excited about and I'm glad I'm a Falcon What are your feelings right now? >> Man, I'm feeling blessed, man. That's that's that's the only word that's really coming to my mind. Um, you know, it was it was a crazy process, stressful process, honestly. Um, but, you know, everything happens at the right times and on God's timing. So, uh, you know, very, very blessed for the opportunity that they've given me and very appreciative that, um, you know, they're believe in me and believe in my abilities that I can bring to the organization. >> Congratulations, man. It's good to have you around still and uh super going from Georgia to here just what uh how can you put into words and kind of describe what that moment was when you get the call and you see it's the Falcons. >> Yeah, it was surreal. Um you know, just because of how everything, you know, has been transpiring, everything like that. Um you know, and and just waiting on your name to get called and you really never know. Um and that's and that's the thing. But it was just crazy. I was actually uh you know, I'm miked up and things like that. I'm like, "Hey man, like can you take my mic off for a couple minutes or whatever the case is?" Um, then I start getting the call. I saw the area code. I said, "Whoa, is this a Georgia?" I said, "Fuck my mic back up, man." So, we we had to we had to do that real quick. But, um, you know, it was just special just because, you know, my brother has another year at Georgia as well. Um, you know, it's easy for my parents to be able to watch both games. Um, so, so that just shows how God works. Um, you know, and I'm meant to be in Atlanta. Zachariah, um, it seemed like you went a little later than a lot of people were expecting and you mentioned maybe this is a little kind of a tough day. What was it like to to be waiting and to not know when you might go and probably just see other receivers go before you? >> Yeah. Um, you know, I I just trust in God's plan so much. I mean, I wasn't really harping on, oh, this guy's going before me, this, this, and that. Um, you know, I got to know that God has a plan for my life. Um, and my my journey is gonna be different than everyone else's. So really just keeping that focus um you know leaning on my family and allowing them to you know continuously help me understand that um you know emphasizing that even though I already do but very straight uh faithled family um you know we very based off that. So really just focus on that. Um you know wherever wherever I ended up landing I knew that it was going to be on on God's timing and uh you know he showed me once again that um you know he'll always put me in the right positions at the right times. >> Zach do you know uh do you know Drake London at all? >> Yes sir. is actually crazy. Um, you know, I've been knowing him for for some years now, which is pretty crazy. Um, and I actually got a chance to talk to him not too long ago before the draft. And I actually talked to him and Bean um, you know, not too long ago. They facetimed me and everything like, "Hey man, I Jake was like, I was telling you, I was telling you, um, he's a great player and even a better person as well. Um, so I'm really excited just to learn from him. um you know, he's very successful in this league and um I'm very excited to learn, you know, under him as a rookie and he's been through the ins and outs of of the team and in the NFL as well. So, very excited to, you know, be be a partner um a partnership in his room for sure. >> Has coach Sansky talked to you a little bit about like what kind of role they see you playing this team? >> Um just trying to be a playmaker overall. You know, wherever they want me to be, you know, offense, special teams, whatever it is, I'm willing to do whatever it takes. How do you think your skill set's going to apply now to the NFL level? Obviously, I think last year at Georgia, we saw a lot whether it was screens at the line of scrimmage, everything like that. How do you think uh you'll be able to, you know, elevate all your skill sets here to the next level? >> Yes, I'm very excited. Um, you know, very blessed to be in this opportunity. Um, you know, in a system like the Atlanta Falcons, you know, had great visits with the receiver coaches and, you know, just talking football is very, uh, you know, I would say similar to Georgia. So, I don't think it's going to be too much of a transition wise. Uh, given that like a lot of NFL teams use like the same terminology and things like that, but Atlanta's pretty similar to Georgia. So, I'm very excited about that. Um, and just excited to see what the coaches uh, you know, want to do, what positions they want to put me in. >> Zachariah, I wonder, forgive me, the conversation with Drake and Bejian, did that happen before the draft or did that happen today after you got picked? >> Yes, it happened today. Um, you know, I was getting a lot of calls and texts right after. Um, but I saw something said Bejan in there and then I had to after I did the first Zoom or whatever, I typed up Bejian in my messages so I didn't like have to scroll to find it and I clicked the message and it was Drake and Bejian like hey like we're excited for you to come um be a Falcon and things like that and they FaceTime me but I missed their call. So had to call them back. Um you know they were excited and pumped up uh you know getting me out there with them boys and I was just telling like it's an honor you know to be on the offense with you guys and shoot I'm ready to go to work right now. >> What do you think the this offense is capable of doing? You Drake Van Kyle all these guys like what what what's the ceiling for you guys? >> I think it's going to be great. Um you know a lot of those guys are are high character and high talented players as well. um you know, so that's something I'm really looking forward to and that's something that I love to be around like-minded players and people who are striving to be the best versions of themselves um and ultimately help the team as best as possible as well. So, I think the offense could definitely be special. Um and I'm excited to see what what transpires this season. >> Zachariah, um sorry, uh welcome to Atlanta. Uh the Falcons have a a good story history at wide receiver. I'm curious when you were, you know, growing up, were you familiar with with the Falcons? Did you pay attention to Rody White, Julio Jones, Calvin Ridley, those guys? >> Oh, yeah, definitely. Um, like you said, there's a lot of guys, um, you know, who who have been successful in the NFL. Um, like you said, Julio Jones and Calvin Ridley's, a lot of those guys like that have been able to pave the way for the Falcons. And it's actually crazy. I'm kind of getting off topic a little bit, but Matt Ryan, watching him growing up was something that's pretty crazy to me. And to be able to just, you know, be in an organization with him is is pretty special as well. just want to get a chance to learn from him and hopefully I can tap back into those those greats who came through Atlanta, especially at the wide receiver position as well to learn a little bit of something as I step into the league. >> Zachariah, I wonder if you were concerned that the incident on Sunday was going to affect your draft position at all. Did just the timing of that. Were you anxious about that this week at all? >> No, I wasn't anxious. Uh if you look at the the things of what transpired then you'll understand why I wasn't anxious. >> Right. And the Ian and Coach Depaskansky said that didn't affect the way they felt about you at all. Was that what you heard from most teams as? >> Uh, yes. I've heard that from from every team. Nobody was concerned. Um, you know, they know who I am as a person and the character that I hold myself of. Um, and and I think that that was pretty much self-explanatory given the report and everything. >> Yeah. Can you can you share what happened as you as you experienced it? >> I can't, man. I'm trying I'm trying to focus on uh you know getting drafted and being excited for that. So apolog >> the the visit you came here was that a local day or what was were the like how did you get invited out? >> Uh it it was a local day for a lot of other guys but I was a top 30 visit. >> Okay. How do you think Zachariah and Georgia prepared you to be ready for, you know, this moment and to be here for the Falcons? >> Yes, they prepared me a lot. um you know just big thanks to the coaches and everybody throughout the organization who you know just put me in the right positions um you know throughout that whole year and the way that coach Smart just goes about the program um you know he holds everyone accountable not just the players but the coaches as well so um shout out my guy coach Kohley did a great job you know getting me prepared um you know learning the offense things like that Luke Corner Javon Williams there's a lot of guys that you know went into making my process at Georgia pretty easy um and and I'm very grateful for them so I feel They allowed me to have a lot of different resources to, you know, use throughout the whole year and be consistent. I found a consistent routine that worked for myself and I plan on using that. Um, it's crazy because now I'm still in Atlanta. I have my recovery guy already in Atlanta. Like I I got everything there that I already did at Georgia. So, it it's just a blessing, man. So, so shout out Georgia for, you know, allowing me to do so and and just stay stay on that track and get a routine for myself. Who who else is there besides a recovery guy on your on your team? >> I apologize. You said what? >> You mentioned your recovery guy. Are there other people kind of on the team that that you use to to help take care of you, keep your body, right? >> Uh yes. Uh you know, I had a recovery guy. I have O2 oxygen. Um you know, they're a great spot as well. You know, it's like oxygen therapy. Get a chance to speed up the the blood cells and recovery process within your body. Um you know, and then it helps you with conditioning as well. So, um, you know, I have them. They were in Athens, but I'm pretty sure they're it's going to be pretty easy for them to, you know, figure something out, um, since I'm still in in in Georgia. And then, uh, you know, got a chiropractor and things like that. And, um, you know, probably going to add on to to nutrition, um, as well. So, pretty much have everything everything accessed, you know, in Georgia. A lot of relationships built and and I'm excited to continue those. >> What up, man? It's Sh >> going on. How you doing, man? Yes, sir. What up, boy? Uh, >> I know you, uh, enjoyed the conversations you have talking to different teams. What stood out to you the most when you got to sit down with the Dirty Birds, man? >> Man, I think it was just the genuiness of everybody. Uh, you know, like I said, I could just be myself the whole time and that was something that was important for me. Um, you know, just to be able to be in an organization who who would would love me for me. Um, you know, and allow me to be myself and along with uh, you know, utilize me the right way as possible as well too to be as successful as possible. Um, but I just love how genuine the coaches were. Um, you know, and I feel like they were they were chill person, like personalitywise, like they gonna let you be yourself, but when it come down to that business, like, yeah, you better be on your business. And that's how I am. Like, I like to be myself, but when it when it really come down to it, like I'm not playing no games. So, I think we we kind of bonded with with uh with the mindset that we have along those lines and and everybody wants to work together to help each other out. So, so I love that about them. >> What's your message, too? What's the message to the fans, man? I know you're a guy who uh love playing to the fans and uh having a good time for fans who may not know what Zack Branch is all about. What would you say to those fans who are getting ready to get to know who you are? >> Yeah, I just say uh stay tuned, man. I'm excited for the opportunity. Um excited to stay in Atlanta. um you know and I want you guys to uh make sure y'all have fun um you know supporting us and and I just want to uh say that you going to get a consistent person, consistent player, somebody who's disciplined and real serious about their craft. So um I that's all I want to say to them. So appreciate you guys. >> A lot's been said about your ability in the the offensive game, but your ability in special teams as well. Tell us a little bit about what you can bring as a return man. >> Yes, I think I can bring a lot of different aspects overall, you know, on offense and special teams like you said. Um those moments are definitely super important to be able to flip the momentum of a game. Um you know, somebody may have just scored a touchdown and then they do a kick return or whatever the case is and sure you take it to the house or you take it past the 50. Now it's like dang like they just switch the whole momentum of the game. Like the whole the sideline that can do something to a sideline. So um whatever position the coaches want me to be in, you know, to contribute to the team and I'm all about winning. Um you know, that's that's what I loved about Georgia as well. everybody loves about um you know trying to win and things like that. So you know whatever position they want me to be in to be able to help our team win is is what I'm going to do. So the special teams receiver, I'm with it all. >> And the NFL has the the kind of the wonky return rules. I mean I mean what are you expecting from that? >> Yeah. Um you know I'm I really like to apply myself. So, I'm going to learn all the rules and things like that and take a lot of time to, you know, learn the ins and outs of that and then, you know, use the events as well, you know, to try to learn to see their experiences. Um, you know, because they were once in college where the rules were different, um, at kick return and then their transition to the NFL or even they were in the NFL and it was before the rules and then now it's new rules. So, just trying to learn from a lot of different people. Um, it's something that's important for me and then um, you know, just try to be the best version of myself every chance I get.

title: Instant Reaction: Bills Select Ohio State CB Davison Igbinosun After Trade Up In The 2nd Round
text: With the 62nd pick in the 2026 NFL draft, the Buffalo Bills select David Igmanos, DV Ohio State. >> Trade alert, the Bills move up four spots into the bottom of the second round to draft quarterback Davidson Ignosen out of Ohio State. Welcome into our NFL draft special alongside a voice of the Bills, Chris Brown. I'm Mattie Glab. Iben Osen is 6'2, 191, long frame, long arms, a speedster, ran a 445 40, and knows how to disrupt routes. Physicality is his game. He's going to get in your face and bat balls down. Why does drafting a quarterback in the second round make sense for Buffalo? Well, I think it was a sneaky need for the Bills because if you look at their current roster right now, the only players on their roster who got on the field last season and played cornerback for this team were Max Haristen and Christian Benford. Duro they picked up in free agency obviously played corner somewhere else. Atlanta he's projected as a possible nickel corner. So outside you really have no depth because Dorian Strong is coming back from a neck surgery. His future is uncertain as far as an NFL career is concerned. There is no determination on his future playing career as of right now. So he's a major if with a capital I. You don't have anyone else. You needed to fortify the depth at the cornerback position and the Bills felt it necessary to trade up to get Igbonosen here and you know he's reunited with Jordan Hancock his former Ohio State teammate. So, I I think it was a need that they had to address at some point in the draft. They choose to do it at the bottom of round two. >> They trade their 66th overall pick. That was their third rounder and their 182nd pick. That's the sixth rounder to the Broncos for 62 to get into the bottom of the second round and pick Ignosen. As you watch his highlights, he flies around the field. He's quick. that 44540 and is a physical cornerback press man is his type of game. How will his physicality fit in to the quarterback's room in Buffalo? >> Well, I mean, he's 6'2, 189, so he's a little narrowframed and I think he does have to add strength and a little bit of bulk uh cuz he's kind of long and lean, but that's what the Bills like. They like length and height uh for corners that play outside for them. Benford's 6'1. Harrison, I think, is an even six foot, but he's long limbmed. And so too is Igmanosen. I mean, he's got 33 inch arms. I mean, that's like offensive line arm length. So, they like long, tall corners outside. He fits the bill there. I think he's got to get a little bit bigger and stronger. You know, run support. Setting the edge out there on the outside is something that he's still learning to be more consistent with in terms of his game. But you're right about him being a press man corner. He likes getting in the face of wide receivers. He trusts his hip flip and ability to turn and plaster in man coverage and will jockey for position all the time. And I think the word to use for him in terms of plant and drive, he's twitchy. Okay? >> Like he can stick his foot in the ground and go in the other direction at the drop of a hat. So when that receiver is stemming his route, he can plant his foot or on a comeback, he can plant his foot, jump the route, make the int. um ultra competitive player. He's the youngest of four boys, six kids total in his family. We're talking about the number one high school recruit in the state of New Jersey. Yeah. >> When he came out for college, went to Old Miss for a year. His defensive coordinator moves on. He wants to transfer, goes to Ohio State when Ryan Day gave him a call. So durable player, 43 straight starts. And the thing that I like is there are plays on the ball. 29 career PBUS in four seasons. That's a fat number playing at a high level of football against some of the best receivers in the country. So, those are encouraging numbers where you got to worry a little bit. 18 penalties the last two seasons. He's grabby and he gets flagged. And it's clear he developed a reputation for being grabby because refs threw the flags on him a good deal. Like 18 penalties in 16 were while in coverage. I mean, that's a problem. So, that's got to get corrected. Um, you can be physical in the NFL. That's a good thing. It's good that he has that. You don't have to coach that into him, but he's going to have to learn the finer points of playing physical while also not drawing flags. That's on his to-do list. >> Four interceptions over the last two seasons. You mentioned that Igmanosen fills in a depth need at cornerback. The question being, you draft depth in the second round. For fans who may not understand why it's important to go that direction in the second round, >> how important is depth in the room right now? >> It's huge. And all I'll do is point to last season. You had Tradavius White out there who played well in the postseason. I'm not going to debate that for a second. He had a nice season uh for them in his comeback season after spending a year away with the Rams and the Ravens. But he gets nicked up in the Denver game. You lose Jammarcus Ingram on a wacky waiver situation. He's in Houston and you have to put Dane Jackson on the field for one play, >> touchdown, and you lost that game in overtime by three. You want better depth that you can turn to. And this is no reflection on Dane Jackson. He played his best. Guys played his heart out when he was in a Bills uniform, but you need higher quality talent, especially at quarterback in a throwing league. Igbonosen is an example of that. Does he have learning to do? Yes. But the elite physical traits are there and you can win with those and get by with those better than a seventh round pick. They felt they had to address it. They did it here. Check cornerback off the list. >> I think that's a great point by you. It's not just depth that you're adding to the cornerback room in Davis and Ignosen. It is better depth. It was a need because of what happened last year. you felt like that position group got really slim at times and you have someone while he does have learning to do can plug and play at times and does add a physicality to the defense. We look at who the Bills drafted 35th overall. They go edge rusher TJ Parker out of Clemson. Known for that power, known for that motor, then they go quarterback Ignosen, physicality, a powerful type of player. What are we learning about this 2026 draft class? uh that they want guys that are going to run and hit. I think that's pretty obvious. Um these are two very physically oriented players, players that like to deliver a blow, I guess, is what I'm saying. Not that there aren't other players in this draft who can do that, but the early indications are Jim Leonard wants a hard-nosed strength, powerbased, physical defense. That's what these two picks say to me in terms of what Jim Leonard is looking for. Speed might not be quite as important up front in particular. You obviously need speed at the corner position, but I think players that bring a physical edge to the field is clearly what he's looking for based on these first two selections on the defensive side of the ball. >> It seems like this coaching staff wants players where in their head, their mindset is we're going to be game wreckers and we're going to impose our force on you. We're going to make a difference in this game. And that's kind of what Parker and Igmanosen seem like based on their tape and based on some of the traits that we already talked about. You spoke about how he matches back up with defensive back Jordan Hancock who played at Ohio State. Hancock and Ignosen over overlapped for two seasons 2024 2025. Ohio State wins the natty in 2024. You're also getting a player who plays against really good talent and knows how to win at the highest level. >> Yeah. And I think the thing that encourages me is while he has to get bigger and stronger to help a little bit better against the run, he played in a conference where there is a lot of running of the football. Michigan runs the football, Iowa runs the football, Michigan State runs the football. Like there's a lot of teams in that conference. The reason that it's viewed as something he has to work on is because there's enough tape evidence of him defending the run where in other conferences, you know, out west in particular, they throw it all over the place. you never see a corner make a tackle in the run front. So, he's been exposed to it. He's still learning on how to be better and more consistent at it, you know, and I think with the quarterback and DB coaches you have here like Mike Dana, who's a good developer of talent, Jay Valai, the new quarterback's coach, you know, who who enforces and prioritizes defending the run on the edges, you know, I think he's going to get the right coaching to get better in that area. Buffalo had a talented pass defense last year at the top of the NFL. They add some new players to the mix this year. No more Taran Johnson. D. Alfred walks into the building. CJ Gardner Johnson as well as you look at the defensive backs group as a whole. What are you learning about the type of ball they're going to play and how versatile it could be? >> Yeah, I I think they want to play angry. I mean, CJ Gardner Johnson is one of the best trash talkers in the league, but he brings the physicality to back it up. Um, there are people with their head on the swivel on offense when they're facing CJ Gardenner Johnson cuz they might lose their lunch um if they're not paying attention. I think Ignosen has that same onfield disposition. Um, maybe he's a little quieter as a rookie, but I think he wants to make an impact early and often. So, while they have a lot of good character players on this roster, I think they wanted more players with an edge to their game. And we we heard TJ Parker tonight say, "When I get on the field, I want to bring the pain." We know how Imanosen plays. We know how CJ Gardner Johnson plays. So, I think these are examples of what they're trying to institute on the defensive side of the ball. They want an intimidation factor on that side of the ball. So, opposing offenses are looking over their shoulder wondering if they're going to take an extra lick, you know, or if they have enough space to catch the ball and then run or are they going to get blasted. That goes along with one of Joe Brady's new sayings, which is you have to play us. It also makes sense with put the ball down. It doesn't matter where we play, when we play, we're going to be ready to get after it and we're going to play hard.

title: Chris Brazzell II introductory press conference | Carolina Panthers
text: First off, congratulations. >> Thank you. >> And we're so happy to have you here in the Carolinas. >> All right, we're gonna kick things off with Cassidy Hill. >> Hey, Chris. Congratulations. >> Hey, how you doing? Thank you. >> Doing good. I have to ask, we saw a picture from back, I think it was in 2021, and you were wearing a Carolina Panthers jacket. What? Like, why? How did you find yourself in that jacket back in 2021? >> I've been a fan. I'm I'm a long time Panther fan. Man, I've been a Panther fan since third grade. So, just a dream come true. >> What led you to becoming a Panthers fan in the third grade? >> So, I play for a team called the Greenwood Panthers. Uh, I wore a jersey that had Panthers on it back in the day. Cam Newton was quarterback. Uh, y had Luke Keat Lee, y'all had Stephen Smith, Steve Smith, y'all going Josh Norman, y'all was going to Super Bowl. I played quarterback at the time. Cam New, they my favorite players of all time. So, I just I kind of just roll with it. Blue is my favorite color. So, I literally just roll with the Panthers and I never look back. >> I mean, like you said, kind of because of that, this is a dream come true. Did you imagine that this is where the night was going for you? >> Uh, no, I did not. Uh, I I ain't know what was going to happen to be honest, but I'm glad this happened. >> Well, congratulations. >> We'll go with Sheena Quick. >> Hi, Chris. Congratulations. I'm Sheena Qu. Welcome to Carolina. >> And I kind of kind of wanted to piggyback on what Cassidy asked you. Um, can you just kind of walk us through what this process has been like for you all the way up until getting that phone call from the Panthers? >> Uh, the draft has been stressful. I ain't going to lie to you. Draft was crazy. I've been anxious. I was nervous. I didn't think I was going to get drafted the third round. So, for my favorite team to call me and select me is like just takes everything away. Thank you, >> Basher. >> Hi, Chris. Bashtart with Carolina Blitz. Congratulations again. Uh, you did your 30 visit here in uh you did a 30 visit here. Just tell us about that. The interaction with Dave and Dan and the vibes you got while you were here in Charlotte. >> Uh, I mean, one, like I said, thousand times my favorite team. So, this visit was the visit I was looking forward to the most. I got there, met the receiver coach, great guy. Met the GM, great guy. Met the OC, great guy. Met the head coach, great guy. So, Bob was amazing. Uh, I feel like my 30 visit paid off for them selecting me. So, >> you're going to be playing with Bryce Young. Uh, what are your thoughts on him? >> Uh, I mean, I went to Tennessee, so he went to Bama, so uh, no shade, but I remember watching Bryce Young when in 2022 when Tennessee beat Brass Young. Brass Young was balling though. Brush Young will balling. He's probably the most underrated quarterback in the league and I didn't want to take some stress off his shoulder to be honest. >> Thank you, >> Scott. Balor. >> Uh, yes. Congratulations to you. Um, we understand you're super fast. I wonder if you could describe your speed to us. >> Uh, I wouldn't say super fast, but I mean I'm pretty fast. Uh, yeah, I ran 437. Uh, I kind of fall started. So, I really could have ran like a 434 or a little slower or a little faster than that. So, y'all going to see my speed for sure. I'll leave it like that. >> Tell us a little bit more too about your playing style in general. How would you describe it? >> Uh, I'm a deep threat. Uh, I love manto man coverage. Uh, I'm a playmaker. You get to throw the ball my way. I'mma go get it. Uh, and that's me. I'm a playmaker. I'm a guy you can count on third and three, third and eight, third and 20. I feel like I'm a guy who's a gonna make a play. So, uh, last thing for me, but Monroe Freeling is from Georgia, and I know that Georgia and Tennessee have a little rivalry. He's their first round pick here. Offensive tackle. You going to get along with him? Okay. >> Uh, what school you went to? >> Georgia. >> Uh, yeah, we should get along good. Uh, they beat us a couple times, but I had a great game, so I'm sure mutual respect between us. >> Thanks, >> Joe Pson, followed by Jeff Hawkins. Chris, congrats, man. >> Thank you. Thank you. >> Hey, um, wanted Canales had an interesting breakdown of you. He said you are one of the few deep ball guys that lands on your feet and you have really good balance and come down with those, not just with the ball, but on your feet. How are you able to do that, >> man? I'm just I don't I don't know. Just God uh given ability. Uh when the ball's in the air, I go, I don't really think when the ball's in the air, I just my body reacts to it and I feel like my body just allows me to land on my feet. So, it's just natural to me to be honest. >> And did I hear you say you had a little bit of a false start or it would have been like a 434? >> Yeah, I would have been uh Yeah, I moved uh you know the combine, the laser, they get you off any movement. So, I move slightly and before I even get to running, it's like point4 seconds already before I get to moving. So, it would been a fast 40. I was trying to go again, but uh had a few phone calls with some guys. They recommended me not to go again, but I was trying to get my 40 down from a 437 to a 434 or 433. Then also uh obviously they took a receiver the last couple years. Last year, uh McMillan rookie of the year. What do you think about joining this room and what do you bring that maybe they don't have uh currently? >> Uh he's been a dog for Arizona. Uh he's he's been a playmix Arizona. Uh he won off the player of the year uh rookie this year. So uh I'm most respected him. He's a dog. Uh I plan on learning from him and hopefully he teach me some things. Uh I hope I just add uh the deep ball out there. Hope they add a playmaker. Uh not even just deep ball out there. Uh I I feel like I can do anything. So hopefully him on one side, me on the other side, we can just make things work and be unstoppable. >> Thanks. >> No problem. Hey, greetings. Um, and congratulations. >> I Hey, I just wanted to follow up on your uh your Cam Newton fandom. Um, >> what what was the one play that you remember that that made you a fan and and what and what did you learn from watching him play? >> Uh, I I wouldn't say one play. I say one I knew him was a good teammate. Uh, for sure. You saw him giving the ball to the kids uh every game. Great guy. Uh, shoot. just a celebration, just him getting dabbing, whipping, hitting the Superman, just him being a a fun guy to watch. It made me fall in love with him. >> Um, have you adopted any kind of celebration yourself or or anything to >> to pay homage to uh to Newton? >> Uh, I have not. Uh, I just kind of uh I just kind of go with the flow to be honest. So, >> Gotcha. Hey, good luck to you. >> We have time for a few more. We'll go >> Yeah. I got so enthralled with your Panther story earlier, we forgot to ask about another one. Um, your dad had a pretty interesting road to the NFL as well. >> And what kind of advice has he given you? How much has he helped you prepare for for this moment and and maybe kind of getting to live out his dream as well a little bit? >> Uh, I wouldn't even say live out his dream. I feel like he he had his dream. He went to live he played a couple years. So, I'll say it's definitely his dream to see me in the NFL. Uh, but I've been getting NFL training since I've been a little boy. Uh, since I I grew up playing football. He was in the NFL when I was born. So, I mean, I just grew up playing football. Uh, found found a love for the game and football at a young age. So, yeah. >> Is there something that he was able to teach you when you were young that that really kind of helped you lock in and you feel like it's helped you get to this point? >> Uh, just my work ethic. uh the little thing like talent's cool but the work ethic and what you do to be better than the guys is what makes you great. >> And then just one more for me. Have you been to a Panthers game before? >> Uh I have not been to the Panthers game. The closest thing I've been to I played uh what's the rivalry? >> Uh Tennessee versus NC State. We played at Bank of American game was playing at the stadium. >> Pretty cool. You'll your first one will be you'll play in it. >> Yeah, it's crazy.

title: Dan Morgan and Dave Canales NFL Draft Day 2 press conference | Carolina Panthers
text: All right. All right. So, uh, first off, uh, jacked about tonight and, uh, being able to get Lee Hunter and Chris Brazzle. Um, two guys that we obviously thought very high of, uh, start off with the lead just like big physical point of attack guy who's athletic enough to get up and down the line of scrimmage. uh makes a lot of plays, uh eats up a lot of blockers for the linebackers, a guy we're really excited about. Uh Chris Brazzle, obviously a big long linear receiver with a big catch radius. Uh can adjust really well downfield. Uh he's got the speed to take the top off, take it the distance. Um so another guy again we're extremely excited about. Um good day. Um work's far from over. Um but yeah, we're we're headed in the right direction. We feel good about the draft so far and you know, we're going to keep building and adding pieces and and following the board and um you know, because that's what we've really been doing up to this point is just kind of following the board and uh letting that kind of guide us. >> Why'd you get straight up? >> You want to say anything? >> Sorry. Oh, just yeah, I'm just excited about the guys and and again just committed to the process of taking the best player on the board and um you know we couldn't pass up an opportunity for a violent player like Lee and then uh Chris, you know, he's one of my favorite players in the draft. um just his film over the last two years, you know, um when you look at two lane and then you look at Tennessee and you kind of combine all of it, you're going to get a full picture of a route tree, uh body control, ability to do those things. And of course, just the ability to stretch the field and um and really put stress on teams uh from a vertical standpoint. And so, you know, we weren't expecting Chris to be there. You know, we were sitting there waiting and he's he just kept, you know, dropping right to us. And um just what a great opportunity for us to just again just add to that room just another element, another dimension and uh and create a competitive roster. >> Let's go ahead, Mike. >> Sure. Uh what made you guys trade up a couple of picks to to get Lee? >> Um the board was kind of thinning out at the time. Um, we just felt like, hey, like this is like the last guy that we kind of had a little at in the higher rounds and we just felt like, hey, let's let's go get our guy instead of kind of settling for somebody else. We're like, let's go get our guy. Uh, we were all convicted on him. Uh, not only as a player, but as a person. Do you see him as being a nose that can kind of complement a rotation of Turk and Bobby or how how do you how do you guys view him from a from a style standpoint? >> Yeah, let's get him in here and see what he can do. You know, um just in our schemes and and uh that part will make a lot of sense for us. But when you're an interior defensive lineman, it all starts with violence and uh that's one thing that he kind of characterized himself, you know, what's your play style? violence, you know, and repeatedly said violence, you know, just um you know, just the way that he's disruptive and um and explosive at the line of scrimmage and then we'll figure out the pieces from there. But we have a really good group in there uh versatile guys that uh we can use in different ways. >> Yeah. And I would add too like the way that we play our Dline like >> there's really not like starters like you know we're rotating a bunch so he's just going to be in that rotation. He can play nose, he can play a little DN in the 34. Um, so he brings a lot of versatility. >> Were you concerned that the Jets might take him 50? >> I was a little concerned that, you know, Dline's pretty thin this draft. Um, so I I felt like, hey, let's let's go get our guy. Let's make sure we get who we want and that's why we traded up and got aggressive. >> The first two picks obviously on the line. What does that say about, you know, was that something you really wanted to address coming in? Yeah, I think uh you know, coach and I and and the rest of the staff like we believe in building building it up front and and winning the line of scrimmage and and I think if you can win the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball, you have a chance to win every single game. So, yeah, that's definitely a point of emphasis. Dave, uh, you haven't had a guy with this type of speed in this offense, uh, so far, a guy that can, you know, get downfield, like you said, vertically consistently. What is it about a guy that has that type of size and speed that makes him so dynamic outside of the route tree that you >> Well, it's the ability to uh take those traits, but then also to play the ball in the air. Um, one of the things that Chris showed is his ability to play the deep ball, land on his feet, finish the play. Um, that's something that's very rare where a lot of times you'll see a guy high point a ball, lay out for it, they end up on the ground. Um, he's just got a special balance with how he finishes, which translates that speed and that size, you know. Um, so just all those things, you know, and and and we've seen how we've been able to use Xavier, T-Mac, Jaylen, you know, with all the uh intermediate stuff and have gone down the field a little bit, you know, and taken some opportunities, but, you know, I think about the space created when they know this is a real burner um and what that does to safeties, what that does to corners and just creating space um for the whole group. >> You mentioned a few guys in that wide receiver room. Can you have too much talent in in a room? >> Absolutely not. You you just, you know, you continue to add great players and and it elevates everybody's play. Um how that plays out, we'll see. You know, there's a lot of work that's got to be done from now until we start the season. And um it's just great to continue to add those guys so that we have different elements and and increase the level of competition in the room. >> You call Chris one of your favorite players in the draft. Was there a particular game, particular play that kind of pops in your mind that you kind of point to and say that's who this guy is? >> Um, I can't say anything specifically, but just the body of work, his ability to have the vertical speed and threat, but then his his ability to drop his weight, get in and out of breaks really efficiently is one of the things that I was so impressed with. And um, you know, in our conversations, you know, as we were going through the process, I was like, "Guys, look at this." Typically, when a guy's 6'4, they don't have that type of bend and flexibility and power to stop on a dime and get out. That's really valuable when you're a vertical threat. Um, because it's a two-way go for you at that point. And then, of course, it was just the uh the acrobatic body balance and ability to stay on his feet to track the ball down the field um that I really just uh fell in love with, you know, and uh and looked, you know, was really excited to get an opportunity to work with those skills. >> You guys had him in on a 30, I think. >> Yeah, we did. What was that visit like with him? >> It was great. It was great. Uh, you know, great personality. Uh, obviously another guy that loves football and, you know, he bleeds it. And I think on our call when we called him, you could hear the excitement in his voice about coming here and competing and adding to that wide receiver room. >> Any texts from Bryce tonight about Brazil? >> I haven't looked at my phone yet. I haven't looked at my phone yet, but I'm sure I'm sure Bryce will be happy about that. >> Dave, your um your response or assessment of the in-person visit with Chris? >> Yeah, so we had him at the combine first. Um and and then we brought him in for the 30 visit, get to spend a little bit more time. And what impressed me about him is just when he talks about what he was working on, that's something that's really big for me, having receiver coaching background. Um, when I can hear a guy talk about the the different skills that they're working on, the drills they're doing, um, he's got a he's got a brother, you know, and like they're doing one-on- ones and they're he he loves the game. He's a um he's about his craft and you can see that on the field. You can see how um how compact and and efficient he is with his footwork and different things. But that always impresses me when a guy has a plan for what they're trying to improve upon. Dan, there are so many kind of players that fit what you guys want to do that got a lot of hype entering the draft. Is there originally it felt like you were going to come in after the end of the third round? Why did you guys kind of stop and come up now as opposed to maybe tracking the rest of the draft possibilities and today? >> Why did we come up in the >> like the draft is still going on? >> Oh, got you. Yeah, I mean there's still guys out there, but you know, we traded up once and obviously we had to give one of our fives and um we got a six back, but you know, I think um in our situation like we feel good about where we're at and what our board looks like and and we'll be ready for tomorrow. >> I think you're averaging like 6'2, 63 in this receiver road now. What kind of how important was it to establish that identity and what does it do for your offense to have a receiver like that? >> Just great players. Uh we're not really necessarily trying to set a prototype. We just happen to continue have opportunities to bring in these massive men, you know, and um all the way down to Bryson Tumine who's 6'5 and goes about 220. You know, they're they're uh these guys are rugged in the run game. That's really important to us. That's something that that Brad uh harps on that Rob Moore is really serious about. Um because we know we're going to run the ball and um and that length and size does help us with some of the different things uh that we do with the run game. And then of course just like uh creating an advantage, you know, um as a target when you when you have that type of size and length, you know, length is very forgiving in terms of getting body position and finishing on the ball. And that's what we've seen out of our guys. Um being able to make those plays in contested situations and and now we got a guy who's who's tall and he's also really fast, you know, and so uh his length and all those things will continue to help him and the speed. Also >> along those lines, there was a lot of speculation that you guys wanted like a yards after catch guy, somebody you could also involve in the run game from a receiver standpoint. Was that a thing and it just didn't quite fit with with your board? >> Um, I think he does have a little run after catch. Um, you know, obviously he's got the 437 speed. Um, so he is a guy that can, you know, if he gets it and he hits a crease, he has the speed to take it the distance. And, um, you know, where we're at making the playoffs and kind of being a little further back in the order, obviously that's going to limit you and, you know, who's going to be available to you as well. So, um, we're just jacked that we could get Chris there at the end. Maybe not a position of need, but is there a certain position in this draft that's kind of gone differently than maybe you had projected or or maybe a trend that you've noticed in these first three? >> Yeah, I mean, I think you just see, you know, once uh like the tight ends, like the tight ends went on a run there for a little bit. The wide outs started kind of going on a run there towards the end when we picked Chris. Um, so yeah, I mean I think you know once one guys starts getting picked and I think teams start seeing guys fall off the board kind of makes everybody a little antsy and you know they start picking that position. So um I don't know if there's one particular position but I think you know once you see you know a particular guy come off the board I think teams get a little spooked and um and they'll go on runs. Dan, as you look at the as you look at the roster as a whole, and as it's got better and deeper, does it change the way you look at day three of the draft, just in terms of how guys fit, whether they make the roster, that kind of thing? >> Yeah, I think uh the big thing is going to be how can guys contribute on special teams. Um, you know, we we only have a certain amount of guys we can dress on game day. So, you know, these guys, you know, here towards the end of the draft, they're going to have to be good teamers, you know, to be able to make our team and and contribute the way we want them to. >> Does that look like linebackers and safeties, tight ends? >> I mean, yeah, it could be it could be a combination of of guys. That's a good try, though. >> No, team. >> Yeah, definitely. Yeah, it's um yeah, usually linebackers, tight ends, it can be corners, safeties, you know, returners, you know, so we'll explore every option and, you know, we'll pick the right guy for us. >> Does Chris have any He doesn't have any return background, does he? >> No, he's No. >> Yeah. >> All right, everybody. Good. Thank you. >> Thank you. Appreciate it. Nat.

title: Lee "The Fridge" Hunter's welcome call with the Panthers | NFL Draft
text: [applause] >> Hey, congrats, man. We're excited to get you. >> [laughter] >> Hey, I'm going to pass you off to our owner, David Tepper, okay? All right, man. Hey, Lee, how you doing? Pretty good. Pretty good. Where you sitting right now? All right, very good. Good. They excited about Carolina? All right, glad to have you, okay? I'm going to pass you over here. Glad to have you. So, um, we stuck to the board. Um and then when you are 190 195 there's a level of breaking tackles um and kind of getting through some of that trash. I mean, just, you know, if you go through his tape and and you cut down into the running back stuff, um, for his entire college career, his ability to run in between the tackles is really good, too. title: Andrew Berry Press Conference: "A lot of action, a lot of movement"
text: We're uh we're excited about today. Um you know, not just with the players that we added, the three guys that we added, but um also how we were able to add to our um our resource base uh in 27 um and then how we're positioned for for tomorrow afternoon. Um you know, with several other day three picks. So, uh obviously a lot of action, a lot of movement um you know, throughout the evening tonight, but we're pleased with where we ended up. And so with that, I'll open up with questions. >> And I'm sure you didn't come into thinking you'd make this many trades, but when you get a sense that it could be just that kind of night for you. >> It's usually just based on the action that you get or how the board falls. Um, I'll be honest, Dan, like we're pretty like we try to stay pretty nimble and flexible just because you never know, you know, when the next opportunity is going to come up. I think that's actually one of the benefits of having volume and quality with your picks because there are more opportunities to maneuver up and down the board. That being said, were you surprised with some of the guys that fell in your lap like Denzel Mos to begin with? They were first round projections. >> I was probably most surprised with Eman. Um, you know, we figured that Denzel could go anywhere from late one to to early two just to be truthful. Um, but Eman, he wasn't someone that we anticipated being, you know, being there as late as he was. So, um, when he got within striking distance, you know, we felt the move was appropriate. You know, to be truthful, he was in play for us at 39. um look at what you did with your wide receiver room. Can you sort of talk about what you have globally from your pass catching core right now and how this might impact like a Jerry Judy or or anybody like that? >> Zero impact on Jerry. He's our bellcow. Um we feel like we have a nice uh I think with receiver rooms you can have, you know, maybe a ball dominant player or you can essentially build a basketball team, you know, with different skill sets. Um you know, we prefer the the second approach. Now, don't get me wrong, I'll take Calvin Johnson if he's if he's out there, but um we feel like we have a nice, you know, well-rounded room with speed, rack, um contested catch ability, separation. Um so, we're we're really pleased with um you know, the youth and talent in that group. >> On that on that trade, >> uh for Emanuel, do you get a sense that another team is going to take or when do you know when to pull the trigger on that? So there they're there they're there probably two separate situations, Jeff. Um one is when you and one is when you do have maybe an inkling that you know you're going into a a stretch where um you and a player or a group of players you know will be target for several teams and you're trying to get ahead of it. Another may just be um and I would put like the Emanuel trade and then what we did for J in 2021 in this bucket where you have a player that you just didn't expect to be in a certain range of the draft and there's a certain level of like okay you don't necessarily have a a team identified that's going to take that player off the board but you look at your resources and say hey this is a price that I'm I'm willing to pay for this skill set for this guy um relative to what you think you're getting. I'll go here and then I'll go Ashley. Y >> you talked last week before the draft just about that positionless defense. Um where does where does a player like Emanuel Warren sort of fit into to that that idea as you think about what you got in him as a player? >> Yeah. Well, I Emanuel is incredibly versatile and and you know, we're um realistic that you're not going to put everything on his plate his rookie year. Um, but I think you really started seeing this with the safety positions, certainly with what Baltimore did with Kyle Hamilton a couple years ago. Um, you look across the league and you see uh just the increase of three safety packages. You look at what um you know, Emani, Nick Mory did for for Seattle this past year and it just gives you a lot of flexibility where you have safeties that can play deep, they can play in the box, they can live in the linebacker world, they can live in the the the nickel world and um they just give a lot of flexibility for a creative coordinator. >> Remember last year after you guys drafted Carson, you talked about the importance of taking an off ball linebacker that high because you hadn't made a major investment there since like four years prior. Um you know Grant we I mean we took him my first draft. We extended them. Um you know Rocket he's outperformed how we acquired him signing him as an undrafted free agent. um Emanuel, it was I mean it we just viewed it as a fantastic opportunity and someone who could you know not only just from a pure talent standpoint improve the room but could also complement our existing core there. Andrew, >> um uh you spoke back in January about dedicating a lot of resources to remaking this offense >> with one day still left in the draft. Um and then like I was actually even thinking um and this this one didn't maybe work out quite as cleanly but even the years where we were short first round picks you know one of those trades was for Elijah Moore and then you know trading down from two for Elijah Moore and then uh taking set in three. That's that's that's, you know, I guess full stop. Doesn't matter who's in the room. If there's a quarterback that we'll like that's available to us at the right cost, um, we'll add that player. Um, you know, that being said, the three guys have done a really nice job so far this spring. You know, we're lucky that we got three days on the grass. Um, you know, they all are are learning the offense quickly. Um, you know, working through their mistakes, throwing the ball, throwing the ball well. I mean, just I, you know, seems like four players that a lot of people had first round grades on and you know, I know a couple years ago with JK, you felt like you got one there, but it feels like you got two of them here. >> Yeah, I I think um you know, as we worked through scenarios, as we worked through simulations, uh we did have simulations where the receivers kind of lined up the way that they did um just because of the strength of this class. So like sometimes you get um a situation actually probably the first time I started calling it was that when we um moved back in it's actually Sashi I think we moved back in 17 um picked up a future one and I think we moved back up for for David at the end of one. title: Reactions to Minnesota Vikings Second & Third Round Draft Picks | 2026 NFL Draft
text: The Minnesota Vikings coming into the 2026 NFL draft had needs at Dline, Oline, safety, cornerback, and wide receiver. In day one and two of the NFL draft, they addressed most of their needs already. You went out and got two DTackles, Caleb Banks and Dominique Orange. Uh, this is a guy that doesn't have a ton of stats when you look at him, but team first guy, unselfish guy, project, big body type, space eater. That's the things you need in a three- four defense. You might not need a superstar right away. You just need a guy that can play within your scheme. And I think this is what Brian Flores renown did with with Caleb Banks. You got Jake Golday, linebacker out of Cincinnati. He's long. He's versatile. He was a former defensive end. So, he understands setting the edge. He understands contain. You put him off ball, and that's what Cincinnati did. This is a guy that if he probably plays off ball, rush outside linebacker his entire career, he's probably a first round pick, but he's learning the position and he does it really well. He can play in the A gap, the B gap, the C gap. You see him lined up in the wide nine. You see him lined up uh back in the in a true like three, four type of look where he's one of the middle, the mic or the mole linebackers and he dissects and reads really well coming downhill, you know, getting through lanes, getting skinny, but also off the edge rushing the quarterback. He has that violent hand. Knock the guy's arms down, get to the quarterback quick, swipe and try to get a strip sack. So, he looks like he looks the part. And uh when I when I look at him, he's wearing number 11, of course, so it reminds me a little bit of Anthony Bar. Um but you look at Caleb Tyranninan, big 67, 323 pound offensive tackle.
