And you know, I wore that on my sleeve and I knew who I was and I I knew regardless of where I'm at, you know, the NFL will find me. My mom was like, you know, don't chase the money, son. The money's going to come. >> Yeah. Not a lot of Georgia State products in the NFL, but there's already one here in Tampa in Venture. >> Big Ben. >> What's it going to be like to reunite with him and have familiar face when you get here? >> Yeah, definitely. I know he, you know, picked it up and he has been blessed to make the opportunity at a 53 man roster. So, you know, if I could soak up any game just from an older guy, I know he kind of, you know, probably going about the right way to handle his business. If I could soak up any knowledge from him, definitely looking forward to that. you've made a lot of catches of 20 plus yards. Um, you know, giving your team an opportunity to score very quickly, you know. Um, just what what's that like for you when you have the ability to just in in a split second, you know, change kind of the trajectory of a game, the outcome of a game with one big play? What's that like for you? >> Yeah, man. I say my prep preparation coming into the game, you know, I I try those things. I practice really hard. you know, you know, when the opportunity comes, I feel like I excel. You know, luckily, I've been surround surrounded by great people who who had my best interest, and you know, my game was definitely not founded, and they helped me polish polish my game. >> Where did your contested catch ability come from? How did you hone that? >> Yeah, I'll say that that's more so of, you know, playing multi sports, playing basketball a lot. I'm a big fan of basketball and, you know, just being a guy who goes up and get the ball as a rebound. That's kind of how I think of, you know, just a jump ball. I'll say, >> as far as wide receivers in the NFL or or older guys, who who are some of the guys you study? Who are some of the guys you watch that you maybe model your game after? >> I say T. Higgins, you know, uh, George Pickkins. Um, I like J Mo a lot. you know, a lot of those big guys who can move in and out their in and out their breaks, you know, go get the ball at the same time, maybe catch it at the line of scrimmage and, you know, take it to the house. >> Ted Ted, what are your thoughts on catching the football next season from Baker Mayfield, >> man? Man, I I I haven't took a a chance to grasp that in yet. And you know, when I get the opportunity to get there, you know, I'm I'mma be plugged to him and I'm and I'm gonna take, you know, advantage of every opportunity I get. >> We got Chris Godwin in the wide receiver room, IA, Jaylen McMillan, some of those other guys. How excited are you to kind of learn from Chris Godwin and some of these other guys who've had success in the league, especially someone like Amecha Ibuka and TZ Johnson who both had success early on as rookies. >> Yeah, man. coming into this thing, you know, the best feedback I got was from these coaches is, you know, stick to that older guy who does the thing right and and I was really big on, you know, I want to come in and have immediate success. So, you know, I'm I'm going to stay in their hip pocket, maybe be a little annoying at the same time, but I know, you know, these are probably great guys in the room and they're great leaders and and I look up look forward to looking up to those guys and I know I know that's going to help me, you know, expand my game. >> Back to the senior role. What was really an opportunity for you to face tougher competition? Like what was the mentality that you needed to have that allowed you to to success because to have success? Because you know some people they can get overwhelmed in those moments and sometimes they can kind of wilt under that pressure but for you it seemed like you really flourished. >> Yeah man. I say I'm I'm big in my Bible. You know I took that morning and I prayed that day before I even hit the field and I knew everything was in God's hands. you know, uh, you know, I I prepare myself well for for those moments and I've been through, you know, situations, close games, tight games and, you know, I know what it feels like to lose and, um, so anything, you know, I do, you know, I I do it to my best ability and I know, you know, how to how to go about things and I feel like if I give my all, you know, I'm comfortable with that. >> What are some of your biggest strengths and biggest things you're bringing to this roster, do you think? Yeah, I I feel like, you know, I'm a true big body X receiver, but I also can play any anywhere on the field and I'm dynamic. You know, I'm I'm a team player at the same time. If you're asking me to do any role or play any position, I'm going to I'm going to step in and, you know, do my part. >> How are you celebrating the draft? Who are you with today? And and how's it gone for you? >> Yeah, about 40 to 50 family members, close friends that I grew up with. my family, you know. I'm really big on my family, my household, my grandma and cousins and all. They're they're out here and they're excited, man. More maybe more excited than me. >> Yeah. What was the reaction like when you got the phone call? >> Definitely considering your school's history. >> Yeah. Yeah, definitely. Before I even picked up the phone, they already were like pulling out the cameras. They're running up like everybody just getting ready and excited for the moment. Uh, actually I already had got the call before I even, you know, got the chance to see it on TV. So, they were already causing havoc in in the Airbnb and the party and all of that. They were they were going crazy. >> Ted Ted, I'm actually Georgia State class of 2018, so I'm excited to have you come down here. Um, >> okay. >> You are now. >> Hell yeah. You already know what it is, man. Uh, >> so you are the highest drafted player in Georgia State football history. Now, just to come from Georgia State, make history like that, what does it mean to you, especially a program that I know showed you a lot of love the last couple years? >> Yeah, man. I give a shout out to, you know, coach Dale McGee and and my receiver coach Damian Craig, also to Quan Marshall, my assistant receiver, coach, man. They they they had a plan for me and they told me how they felt about me just coming there. They were truth truthful from the beginning and they saw the potential with me and you know they stick stick with me every day and glued to me whether it's words of encouragements or words words I needed to hear. >> Ted, if you had a message for the Bucks fans watching this right now, what would it be? >> Man, y'all got y'all got a dog. I'm telling you you like I seen all these people saying sleep at a drive, man. I'm I'm here for a reason. >> Awesome. Anything else? >> All right, guys. Congrats. Thank you, God. >> Definitely. >> We'll see you in a couple weeks. >> Jesus day. Yes, sir.

title: Mike Biehl Reflects on Day 2 of the 2026 NFL Draft | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: A few people stayed up. That's good. Good to see y'all. Fire away. >> Mike, talk about Josiah Troder. What uh would you like about him? Only two year worth of experience. You see a lot of these college players staying in for five and six years sometimes. What What made him come out of the draft and and what did you like about him? Yeah, I I mean I'll say like this we drafted three 21 year olds, so that's it's been a a rare instance recently with the co stuff, but uh I think Jeremiah, he's just been groomed to to play football his whole life, you know, growing up with his dad and his brother, you know, getting drafted a few years ago. And um he had made a well-informed decision is what I would say. Like he he thought he was ready to come out and we spent a lot of time with him through this process and um his play on the field dictated that too, I think. How much are you influenced by the relationship like with Mike Caldwell and and stuff like that? >> Yeah, I mean I think all that stuff helps, right? Just to try to get to know the player. Um yeah, Mike had a relationship with him. Todd has a relationship with his dad, too. Um you know, and again, we spent a lot of time with him, too, and just came away feeling really comfortable. But I think all that matters, you know, just again trying to find out everything we can about these kids and and uh that played a part in it. the perception is that you guys needed to improve um some of your pass defense inside with with the linebacker position. I know you got picked up some free agents obviously, but like for for Troder seem to be more of a of a run player right now at least, right? >> Yeah. I mean, I I would say that's that's fair, but I also think that he he can play in coverage. I think he's that's a little bit of a misnomer and you know, I don't know if it's the the narrative that the media is putting out, but like he's actually pretty good at it. Now, that being said, he's an old school downhill Mike backer that can play the run, which is hard to find nowadays. I mean, with the college game, the way it's went, it's all lateral and everybody's looking for the speed stuff. And to us, he has enough speed to play in our our league. Um, now, if you said, is he a better run defender than than a pass defender? I would say, yeah, that's probably fair, but we think he has the capability to be a three down linebacker. >> Talk about his blitzing ability in in that matter. >> Yep. And I would say that's that's a big part of his game, too. I mean, he he understands how to rush the passer and and he can go through running back's faces if he chooses to or he can make a miss. So, that's going to be a plus for Todd on third downs. And I mean, you guys have seen the way that he uses our inside backers when Devin was here. And I mean, I would I would anticipate Josiah having a lot of production in that phase >> with with the fact that I mean, he's only had like two years of college ball experience. Would you expect him to kind of grow in in his coverage, in his recognition, and his instincts in that department? >> Yeah, 100%. I mean, all these guys are like, like I said, when I started, we drafted three 21 year olds, and we think the upside with all of them are is is huge. So, um, yeah, but I would say that he also has played the game for a long time and again has been kind of groomed from from a young age. So, he's he's pretty far advanced, I would say, in that in that area. >> I don't know if you could also speak to the the because I I understand he's had a few knee injuries between college. I know in 2023 he had a torn I think it was an ACL and then I think he had like it was an MCL as well or like I mean did you guys feel comfortable? I'm guessing you felt comfortable with the medical. >> Yeah, I mean I would say anytime we get asked a question like that the answer is always going to be yes. We're comfortable with it. Otherwise, we wouldn't even mess around with it. I mean our doctors and athletic trainers, they do a heck of a job and they spend tons of time on all these guys. So if we select somebody, we're we're certainly comfortable with >> it. What do you see out of his maybe leadership potential maybe further down the road? you know, where's the green dot? And, you know, you see him talking to us, especially with the linebacker room that obviously lost a big-time leader, you know, maybe down the line. What do you see out of him in that sense? >> Yeah, I mean, it's I'm never going to compare anybody to Levonte David, first of all, but uh he uh he has those qualities though as far as the potential to be have an impact on our defense and the in the locker room as a whole. Um he's just he's he just gets the game, too. So he's if all the the resources we talked to or the the sources we talked to at the school spoke very highly of him and not only his ability to learn but also his ability to help others learn and he would come in every week and have it like a cheat sheet and tips for the other players in the room and helping them out. So he's well on his way to being a leader now. He's got to get here and and get in the locker room and prove it to the to these veterans. But uh he's got a chance to be pretty good. I think >> Mike, in losing Evans, you guys seem to need a true ex receiver. So, is Hurst obviously fill that role and what is it you you really like about Yeah, >> because your room is >> plentiful as it is. >> So, first of all, with Mike, like we're never ever going to try to replace Mike, but but you do try to replace size and speed, which Mike had, and and we think that Ted has that, too. So Ted's a he's a small school guy that, you know, started out Vald Dasa, transferred to Georgia State. Um, played a couple years there. Had opportunities to go, you know, to bigger schools with the NIL stuff and and stayed loyal to Georgia State, which it's kind of refreshing a little bit in this day and age that uh that guys choose to do that sometimes. Now, you can look at it the other way that he's not choosing to go up and play against the best competition and stuff like that, but a guy like Ted goes to the Senior Bowl and does that and then, you know, proves that he can do that as well. So, he's just kind of checked the boxes every step of the way. Um, and at the same time, he's still has a lot to improve on, you know, the route running, the I mean, he's he's got he's just kind of a raw player, but he's a he's a big fast athletic guy that's willing to learn and and we're excited about him. >> The I mean, for him, is it is it the contested catches? is that I mean I know again there's no replacing Mike but you know he's also that guy that if you need to score quickly and you can get him you know single coverage downfield you know you're taking that shot. Um I know that he has produced a lot of of catches of 20 plus yards. I mean is that kind of I guess what you could envision for him? >> Yeah, I think so. I mean again like we're talking about bringing a guy into a crowded room to use your your quote earlier. I mean, we're not expecting him to come in and just, you know, take over and and have to to be a big part of our offense. Now, that being said, there's nothing that says he can't. If he comes in and proves himself, he, you know, whatever role he has, it's going to be on what he's ready for and how he works and proves himself. But, but yes, he is a big guy that's 6'4, 210 and and runs in the 44. So, that's intriguing to us, you know. Um, and again, the downfield stuff, he's got really good ball skills, too. So, not only can he get over the top and beat guys deep, but if it is contested, he has the ability to make those catches. So, um he's got a lot lot of traits that we look for at at the X position, which is what Mike played, and um and we'll just see how it all all plays out. >> So, a factor like is is a big slot. I know that that Zach likes to use that. That's how we use Drake London and Atlanta quite a bit with slant catches, getting yards after catch with that speed. >> Yeah. I mean, again, like I have complete faith in in our coaches, uh, that they're going to put him in great positions and and I wouldn't rule that out. I mean, I just think that, you know, there's there's three, sometimes four, sometimes five white outs on the field and they're going to put them in spots where they're going to be able to succeed and and he has a skill set to do that. You know, it's just when you see the size and the speed, everybody thinks outside, but we've been pretty successful putting bigger guys inside as well, you know, and Chris can do that, Mecca can do that. like we got some guys that can do it, but if to to get matchups, that's what this game's all about is matchups and and he has the ability to do a lot of different things. >> Do you guys let Jason trade this year? Um how how important was for you guys to get one of those extra day day three picks in >> We were actually joking about that. It was time for us to trade back and get an extra pick with Jason. Uh that's that's always interesting, especially in a draft like this where I think it probably wasn't like topheavy, but I think there's a lot of depth and a lot of quality players in those, you know, mid rounds to even the fifth round, which, you know, we picked up that pick. So, it's always good to get more picks. I mean, we feel like we can we can hit on those later rounds. Our scouting department does a heck of a job of, you know, of identifying those guys that so that we look at them, too. And and uh we've had a pretty good hit rate around here recent. you guys sweating it out as as as 84 came back up and >> uh I mean you're always going to sweat it out. Like that's just kind of part of the draft because you're dealing with 31 other teams that are, you know, doing the same thing you are. So um but at the same time, we trade back. We know that there's a chance we're going to lose him, but so we're always prepared to have other guys lined up if that's the case. But but yes, when uh when our pick came up and he was still there, it was pretty pretty exciting in the room. >> What did you see first in the in the senior bowl? you mentioned, you know, stepping up and playing up against, you know, tougher competition. What What did you see from him there? >> Just his ability to compete and and and hold up versus those guys. Um it wasn't too big for him, which is always kind of what you look for from smaller school players if they can go there and compete and it was like I mean I always use Alli Maretta in a perfect example like Alli went there coming from Hobart College and struggled the first day but by the end of the week he was he was kicking everybody's ass. So that was always it's it's those small school guys that's what they have to do. that first of all, they have to dominate their their level of competition. If they're not doing that, then it's hard to project them in our league. But if they are, and then they can go to the Senior Bowl and or the any of these all-star games really and hold their own, then it gives you, you know, encouragement that they'll be able to do it in our level. >> Mike, last night we saw a pretty excited uh Bucks war room and selecting Ruben Bane Jr., uh what are your thoughts uh overall about being able to land him in the process in which you you got him? >> Yeah, that's that's probably one of the more excited draft rooms I've been around of. I mean, it just when you get a player of his quality, um, where we were picking, I think that's what where the excitement comes from. Um, because a lot of us didn't expect him to be there. We just assumed he was going to be long gone. But again, that's why we prepare for every scenario. And we did a lot of work on Ruben just like we do every other prospect. And, um, it it's just fun to to see him there. Uh, because we think we're getting one of the better pass rushers in this draft. and he brings a lot of attitude and and effort and just some nastiness that we've kind of been lacking a little bit I think on defense and I would say that Jeremiah has that stuff too just what I was talking about the run stuffer downhill type player so uh it's exciting to add those two young guys to our defense >> speak of that you look at edge rusher and linebacker and those were two of the biggest needs coming into this this offseason with Bane in the first round with Troder in the second round how does it feel how for you guys are you comfortable knowing that hey we might have just locked up two starters for the first and and fix this position that was one of the ones that we kind of set into this offse to fix. >> Yeah, I I mean I think that that's what you always go into a draft hoping that the needs match up with the best player and I think that's kind of what happened in this draft. I mean I don't think that Jason we never force things and again I don't think we did this year either. I just think that just happened to be, you know, the best player was there and it's two positions that, you know, I would agree we probably needed to to upgrade a little bit. And um yeah, it's pretty exciting to think that, you know, and we'll see. I mean, it's too early to call them starters, but you're drafting in the first and second round, you're expecting to come in and compete for that role. So, we'll see how it all plays out, but yeah, it's pretty exciting. >> What was what was it that sold you on on Bane? >> I mean, because this is this is a class where there's a lot of of edge rushers and we've seen so many >> so many come off the board. He's different because just because of the body type, you know, he's a shorter, thicker guy, but his his power is unmatched in my opinion. Like he he has the ability to go through blockers faces, which is a it's a good place to start as a pass rusher in our league. I mean, everybody talks about all the speed guys that can can run the hoops, but it's hard to get around Tristan Warfs. I mean, he's just as athletic as a lot of these guys, and it's tough and it's tough to get around him. So, you got to be able to incorporate some kind of power into your game, and he has that already. So now it's just a matter of him continuing to hone his skills and um and be able to to use change ups, which he's already done a lot of. I mean, he had a really good defensive line coach there at Miami, and he's probably pretty far ahead of the game compared to a lot of guys. >> Mike, there were a couple other uh linebackers there for the taking in the second round, but what was the the factor in selecting Josiah over some of the other guys? >> I mean, in the end, it's about the player and the person, right? and we just thought he was one of those guys that matched up with both of them. Like he has, you know, he has a lot of ability to play in this league. And again, I just talked about the toughness and the and the attitude that a guy like him brings to our defense. Um, and then the person and the leader that we think that he could potentially be and the teammate. I mean, he he just fits kind of the the I am that man that we use a lot around here. >> Mike, with with Troder, I think he had 27 reps on the bench at Combine. It's the most by a linebacker in like four years at Combine. I just want to ask you about his physicality and what that brings to the position for you guys. >> Yeah, I mean again I think that's you you don't see that a lot in co the college game now like I said before. I mean it's just the ability to go on and take on these big offensive linemen and use that ability to press and get off blocks. I mean he he's pretty rare in that in that sense from from a college guy coming out like um so he's just to me like he's so much further ahead of the game being able to adapt to a pro style game as opposed to what you know a lot of these guys coming out of college. It's it's probably a bigger learning curve than what he's going to have. >> How do you kind of weigh what his strengths are versus because as he mentioned like there are other guys on the that were still available like CJ Allen he was still on the board I think at the time. Um I know that Jacob Rodriguez was already had already been picked but like how do you weigh like what his strengths are? You know he's a thumper and and very physical uh versus like okay maybe getting more of um like ancilloney type you know where he's more of a of a coverage type of a player. like how did you kind of I guess come to the decision of of which style you wanted, you know, cuz two in free agency, you know, you signed different guys, >> right? >> I mean, there's so many things that go into selecting a player and I would say that we had all those guys pretty closely clumped together. I mean, they're all really good football players. So, um, when choosing one over the other, it just comes down to the conversations that we have as a scouting department and then the conversations we have with the coaches and the comfortability everybody has and and we're so prepared going into the draft that we kind of know the way we're going to take him and and then we just kind of stick to that. But I mean, Josiah, just all the stuff I've already talked about with the the phys physicality, the the the ability to play downhill, the ability to coverage, the ability to blitz, like all those things are just intriguing. And um it was pretty unanimous with the coaches in in the personnel department. >> He's 21, but he only has two years of college experience and and typically you don't see that a lot. Any is he just precocious? Any any kind of trepidation there about a guy that's only played two years college football? No, I mean I I think Rick, we used to see that a lot more. You know, I think the co stuff has changed that. So, we've kind of gotten away from it and you you have a lot of these guys who are, you know, 23, 24, 25 and have bu played for five or six years and um you know, but five, six, seven. Yeah. I mean, like, but that's that's kind of the way the the college game used to be because we had so many underassman coming out and not all of them are three-ear starters. So, >> you saw it a lot more and and again, it's it's it's on a case-byase basis and and I think that Josiah has proven that, you know, he can play at a high level and and uh just from a mental standpoint, again, he's so he's so far ahead of the curve, I believe, >> as far as the way the board plays out, shakes out tomorrow for you guys and some of your perceived needs, are you guys feel comfortable going in tomorrow with some with some of the the spots that you feel like you need to add to? >> Yeah, for sure. And I kind of hit on earlier. I think this is a pretty deep draft and there's a lot of depth that you know at a lot of different positions that and again like we're never going to force things and that's the beauty of tomorrow and and picking up another fifth round pick and maybe we can talk Jason into trading again and get a few more. But um but yeah, that's that's always exciting and and again that's kind of when your your scouting department kind of kicks in in those later rounds and and and uh it's always fun and even going into undrafted free agency like all that stuff is a blast for for scouts. with you guys like being really intentional about the type of like personalities you're bringing in, especially like on defense this off seasonason, wanting those kickers. Um, how did that kind of I guess >> well, I didn't know if I was allowed to say it on here, but like how does that how did that kind of, you know, change like your your draft board? I mean, do you put like maybe this year personality traits uh a little bit higher than maybe you would, you know, ability? Like how I guess I'm curious how that that kind of impacted you guys this year. Yeah, I I think that it's like we we do the same thing every year. And now I shouldn't say that. We we're always evolving, right? Like I mean, we we try to stick to our core principles and bring in the right kind of guys, but at the same time, they they're not all going to be choir boys and and you know, >> watch those last year, right? >> Yeah. Yeah, they are. But they all are competitive. So, and if you look at some of the greatest defensive guys in in Bucks history, they were not choir boys. And >> so, it's it's fine. I mean, and I think we have a really strong um coaching staff, a really strong locker room, you know, that can handle some some big personalities now. And um but we're always going to stick to our core values and, you know, try to bring in the right kind of guys. >> Okay. Thank you. >> Appreciate it.

title: LIVE: GM Adam Peters Speaks to the Media on Night 2 of the NFL Draft | Washington Commanders
text: a lot easier on the west coast. >> Well, thank you guys for for hanging. Um so, um I will start with a little opening statement then and ask you ask away. Um but, uh Antonio Williams, Clemson wide receiver. Um really, uh really really impressed by Antonio. We had him in on a 30 visit and uh really liked him. Uh, you know, Lance Newark and I went out there during uh the season and got a chance to talk to Davo and and Woody McCorvy out there. They spoke extremely highly of him. Um, Dustin Reagan, our area scout, really swears by him. Had a great talk with him before we made the pick. And um, so really a top-notch young man. Uh, super hard worker, consistent, the same guy every day. um high high FBI, can multi-line, understands the game, understands zone, understands a man, understands how to win. Um and he's super competitive and he's super tough. Um played through broken ribs last year in 2024. Really fought through a hamstring injury this year, which which really limited his um you know, his production, but played through the whole thing. So, this guy's a tough kid. when you go back and watch his his 2024 film, you really get to see what what a special talent he is. Um, so, uh, I'd describe him just a just a great athlete. Great athlete, really fast. Um, and he's fast in a lot of different ways. He's fast at the 40 time. The GPS is really, really high on him in game and then the old scouts eye. You see him, he plays fast and he plays at a high level. Uh, he's an NFL route runner. He can win versus press. He can he can beat man coverage. Um and so we really like the versatility of him as well. He uh he can play inside. He played a lot of inside this year. He played outside last year. And that's really the the thing that differentiated him from a lot of guys is winning outside and winning against really good players outside, especially in 2024. So, uh NFL route runner. Um there's just a lot of really really good things about him and uh just all around great package. So thrilled to have him, thrilled to have him at the wide receiver room and um just uh happy good couple days here. So go ahead. >> With the inside outside, how would you project him or see him here and what skills allow him to be productive maybe inside and out? >> Yeah, that's a great question. Well, I think um yeah, if he he can play Z and F and or or you know Z in in slot and so um he'll he'll work at both of those. Uh the things that he can show you he can play outside. He's he's not he's not huge, but he's not small. He's just a hair under six feet and he's he's a really tough player and he's got really good releases and he plays really fast. So those things allow him to win on the outside uh versus versus bigger corners. So even though he's not a 6'4 guy, he can still win on the outside and and his speed and his releases and his route running and his details allow allow him to do that. And the same thing with inside is is he can he can win with his quickness as well. >> Was there a thing that jumped out to you when you were watching him? >> Uh I I think there there's a lot of games. I think the the one that really sold it for me was uh playing Georgia last in 2024 and just seeing him play outside and just seeing how win like uh you see NFL guys win on Sundays. >> You mentioned his route running. What stood out to you on tape about that? >> Just the the speed and the detail and the precision and the quickness in and out of breaks.
